statement: Kernel-checked adaptive final theorem: if 0<theta<1 satisfies PI(theta), then every fixed 0<c<(1-theta)/3 gives the stated prime divisor for all sufficiently large k and 2k<n<=exp(c(log k)^2/loglog k). The older balanced 9/23 endpoint is an artifact. For the explicitly named location-blind, termwise-nonnegative full-tail class, Lean proves the exact block invariant, cardinality tail, weighted extraction, finite endpoint no-go, and a finite source-family map: explicit common raw constants a,En,ED give C=-log(a), D=5/2+En+ED. Thus finite families cannot reach c>=(1-theta)/3 under these uniform raw comparisons and the summed nonnegative little-o ledger. The theorem does not assert that arbitrary shifted/regrouped sources possess those constants. Erdos 451 itself is not closed.

dependency_gaps: The abstract theta theorem assumes PI(theta); the theta=21/40 corollary imports the Baker--Harman--Pintz short-prime input exactly as the source paper does.

The complete adaptive four-range theorem is kernel-checked. For the enlarged no-go, the finite cardinality tail, partition telescope, weighted extraction, block algebra, endpoint contradiction, and source map from fixed raw a,En,ED to C=-log(a), D=5/2+En+ED are kernel-checked uniformly over arbitrary finite index sets. A broader shifted/regrouped source must separately prove that its raw constants are common to the family; the eventual K/loglog(k)^2 limit is not packaged as a Lean sequence theorem.

The no-go is confined to the named location-blind deterministic-tail class whose nonnegative Theorem 4.1 bounds are summed and required to be o(k^theta/log k). It does not cover sparse covers selected from actual prime locations, cross-block cancellation, stronger prime inputs, stronger exponential-sum estimates, or the true bad-set cardinality.
Novelty and publication priority remain unchecked.
